title: Judicial Review, Fundamental Rights, and the Invisible Constitution

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Following the 1989 regime change, the Hungarian Constitutional Court under President László Sólyom was often described as one of the most powerful constitutional courts in the world. Its hallmark in those years was the 'actio popularis': anyone could challenge a law without proving personal standing (the rules have changed since).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Sólyom used the idea of the *láthatatlan alkotmány* (invisible constitution) in his 1990 concurring opinion on the death penalty: the idea that the court draws on a coherent system of fundamental principles that goes beyond the literal text of the constitution.
